data.name: Omkaranath
data.gender_notes: Omkaranath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Omkaranath is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Omkar'. 'Om' is a sacred syllable in Hinduism, symbolizing the ultimate reality or the sound of the universe. 'Anath' means the ruler or the lord. Therefore, Omkaranath signifies the one who bows to Lord Omkaara or the lord himself. The name Omkaranath carries the meaning “Bow to Lord Omkaara” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Omkaranath usually hope their child will grow to embody bow to lord omkaara and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Omkaranath total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

vedic_reference.note: Omkaranath is a form of Lord Shiva, also known as Omkaara Rudra or Nataraja. He is revered as the lord of the primal sound 'Om'.

historical_references.reference: Omkaranath Thakur was a 19th century poet and philosopher in Bengal who wrote in the language of the common people. His works were a major influence on the development of the Bengali language and literature. He is known for his devotional poetry and his philosophical works on Advaita Vedanta.

Omkaranath was also known as 'Omkarnath Thakur Goswami Mahasaya'. He was a prominent figure in the Hindu Tantra tradition, and is believed to have been a teacher and guru to Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. Ramakrishna is known for his teachings on the unity of all religions and the spiritual potential of every individual.
